rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
**Particle-Antiparticle Annihilation:** When a particle meets its antiparticle (e.g., $e^- + e^+$), they annihilate into pure energy (photons).…
**Pair Production (Creation):** The reverse of annihilation: a high-energy photon ($E > 1.022$ MeV) creates an $e^- e^+$ pair near a nucleus (to conserve momentum). The photon must have $E \ge 2m_e c^2$.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Fission vs Fusion in $BE/A$ Context:** Both processes release energy by moving toward the iron peak ($^{56}$Fe, $BE/A \approx 8.8$ MeV). Fission splits heavy nuclei ($A > 56$); fusion combines light nuclei ($A < 56$). Both increase the average binding energy per nucleon of the final products compared to initial reactants.
